thread.title: This stat should have Apple longs feeling confident about their investment - MarketWatch

title: This stat should have Apple longs feeling confident about their investment - MarketWatch
text:
Published: Mar 6, 2018 1:17 p.m. ET Share A report from UBS should have Apple investors smiling. 
By Social-media editor 
The biggest underweight position on the planet: Apple? 
Yes, as you can see by this UBS table cited on FT.com , the $900-billion tech giant isn’t getting much love from fund managers around the world. 
The UBS ranking is calculated by comparing the positions of active managers to a stock’s share of the MSCI World index URTH, +0.27% In other words, Apple is a much bigger part of the benchmark than it is fund managers’ portfolios. 
The surface takeaway is that the pros believe the stock won’t keep up with the broader market, but the Apple AAPL, -0.08% bulls — and contrarian investors — might tell you there’s cash out there ready to flow back in when the timing’s right. 
The thinking: It’s trickier for a crowded stock, like Alibaba BABA, +3.18% on this list, to rally since so many investors have already bought in. On the other hand, there’s more room for an underweight stock to pop when sentiment turns more positive. 
So far this year, it’s been rather ho-hum, performance-wise, for Apple shares, even though they’ve managed to outperform the broad market. 
When a similar reading popped up back in 2015, billionaire activist investor Carl Icahn said fund managers would come to regret it. 
“They are underweight Apple in relation to the index funds, and I think more and more of these funds will realize that’s going to hurt their performance in the future as Apple continues to launch new products in new categories and continues to grow earnings,” Icahn told Reuters in an interview . 
His call was spot on. Since Icahn made that prediction, Apple shares have grown by more than 110%, easily outpacing a 30% increase for the Dow Jones Industrial Average DJIA, +0.04% . Quote References
